children: (Updated to include commentary from Summit Research.)
On Monday, shares of Marvell
and Lumentum
plunged double digits on news that the companies intend to merge through an all-stock deal that values Lumentum at around $115B.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
and Summit Research if they thought the deal was a mistake.
Kenio Fontes: I wouldn’t say that the deal between Marvell
and Lumentum

is necessarily a mistake. There is real long-term potential. As I said in my recent article, it could be accretive for the combined company as the deal unlocks not only cost synergies of around $1B and a larger addressable market but also an expansion of the solution offerings, creating a verticalized AI behemoth.

On the other hand, I’d label it as a complex and high-risk move. There is a lot of complexity regarding execution (systems integration, contract revisions, cultural friction, etc.) and also uncertainties when it comes to other parts of the deal, such as valuation, dilution, and approvals.
So I don’t see it as a wrong strategic vision; I think it could create a better company. The problem may be the timing, valuation, and uncertainties that leave little margin of safety.
Jonathan Weber: I think that the deal between Marvell
and Lumentum
makes sense strategically, as it better positions the combined company as a major connectivity player.

Lumentum shareholders seem to think that Marvell is underpaying, however, and both companies were hit hard by the recent AI sell-off. Valuations for both companies aren't low, which is why I am not especially bullish on either despite the deal making sense from a product portfolio and synergies standpoint.
(Jonathan Weber is a contributing analyst for the SA investing group Cash Flow Club.)
The Techie: The deal was not a mistake as much as it was a surprise to the market. A week ago, we heard rumors about this, and Marvell
crashed while Lumentum
was rewarded. On Monday, Marvell and Lumentum stocks fell 12.7% and 18.6%, respectively. I think what really spooked investors were the details of the deal and the timing.

As I discuss more extensively in my coverage of Marvell, I think the market will continue digesting the news in the short term, particularly the regulatory approvals and dilution impact. I don't think this is the time to run away from the stock. Once these negatives are priced in, which is what we're seeing now, Marvell
will have a clear runway to meaningfully compete in the future of the AI buildout.

Summit Research: The timing and structure of the Marvell-Lumentum deal creates more questions than answers amid mounting uncertainties across the broader AI trade, creating a potential valuation chokehold on both stocks.
On the one hand, it raises questions about Lumentum

management’s confidence in the durability of longer-term optical connectivity and laser demand as CPO becomes the primary architecture in AI systems. Coupled with the extended closing timeline into 1H28, this introduces additional execution and cyclical risks for Marvell
shareholders.

On the other hand, the fixed share exchange ratio creates uncertainty over the actual consideration Lumentum shareholders will receive at closing, exposing them to Marvell-related volatility. This risks suppressing near-term upside despite its standalone earnings momentum amid intensifying laser supply constraints.
